name: CHINA

flag.title: Five-Star Red
flag.note: Red field; large star + 4 small stars

lead: China has more people than any other country. It has the Great Wall, giant pandas and a writing system that has barely changed in 3,000 years. China is so wide that the sun rises two hours earlier in the east.

facts.label: Capital
facts.sub: Home to the Forbidden City palace

geo: The Tibetan Plateau, the 'Roof of the World', fills the west. The air is so thin that visitors get dizzy walking. The Yangtze, Yellow and Mekong rivers begin here among glaciers.
The Yangtze flows east across fertile plains. It is longer than the distance from London to New York. It feeds 400 million people. The Gobi Desert in the north is bigger than Western Europe.
animals: Giant pandas nearly vanished. Careful protection has raised wild numbers to about 1,900. Pandas munch bamboo all day, but it is basically leafy cardboard.
The Chinese giant salamander is the world's largest amphibian. Snow leopards hunt wild sheep on the Tibetan plateau. As few as 4,000 survive.
culture: Chinese New Year sparks the world's biggest yearly trip home. Families set off fireworks to scare away bad luck. Children get red envelopes full of money.
China invented paper, printing, gunpowder and the compass. Sichuan cooking is tongue-numbing hot. Tea was found here 5,000 years ago.
history: Emperor Qin Shi Huang joined rival kingdoms into one in 221 BC. He ordered a wall across the north. He was buried with 8,000 life-sized terracotta soldiers. Farmers found them in 1974.
For centuries China was the richest country on Earth. It sent silk and porcelain along the Silk Road. The People's Republic began in 1949. Now China has the world's second-largest economy.
wows: China shares a border with 14 countries, more than any other nation.
The Three Gorges Dam is Earth's largest power station.
China used more cement in three years than the USA did in the 20th century.
A panda's 'thumb' is really an enlarged wrist bone.
People who speak different dialects can all read written Chinese.
All of China uses one time zone, though it is as wide as five.

myths.myth: The Great Wall is visible from space
myths.fact: Astronauts say they cannot spot it with the naked eye. It is long, but only about 5 metres wide.
Japanese immigrants made the first fortune cookies in California in the early 1900s.
